proposed_excluded.what: 21 scratch Vector3/Quaternion/Euler/Raycaster field declarations in the OnFoot constructor (`this._slideE = new THREE.Euler()` through `this._ray = new THREE.Raycaster()`, foot.js:556-568,573-575,580,585-588), each existing purely so the hot per-frame code below (handsOnLedge, moveAim, rollPose, seatInPocket/moveArm, etc.) can write into a pre-allocated object instead of `new`-ing a fresh Vector3/Quaternion every frame and generating garbage.
proposed_excluded.reason: Concept genuinely absent in C#/Unity, not merely 'done differently': THREE.Vector3/Quaternion/Euler are JS heap objects, so reusing one is the only way to avoid per-frame GC pressure. UnityEngine.Vector3/Quaternion are C# STRUCTS (value types) — a local `Vector3 v = ...` inside any of this port's own methods (MoveAim, RollPose, SlidePose, FacePoint/GripPoint, SeatInPocket, all already ported and claimed under FootAcrobatics.cs/FootController.cs/FootClimb.cs/FootWeapons.cs per this file's own citations) is stack-allocated and costs nothing to create fresh every call; there is no GC-avoidance problem for a pre-allocated field to solve. `this._ray = new THREE.Raycaster()` is the same story one level up: Unity's Physics.Raycast is a static method against the engine's own PhysX broadphase, needs no persistent Raycaster instance, and every use site in this port already calls it that way (ProbeGround/WallHitProbe/FindLedge, etc.). Checked the concept-kept bar directly per docs/port_units/README.md's crane.js precedent before filing: every USE SITE of these 21 scratch fields is a method that already has a cited, claimed C# port (MoveAim->FootAcrobatics.MoveAim, _rollPose->FootController.RollPose, _slidePose->FootController's SlidePose, _handsOnLedge/_facePoint/_gripPoint->FootClimb's FacePoint/GripPoint, _seatInPocket/_moveArm->FootWeapons.SeatInPocket), each written with plain local Vector3/Quaternion values and no persistent scratch field of its own — so the PATTERN these 21 lines exist for was checked against the real ported code, not assumed.
proposed_excluded.excludes_only: the 21 `new THREE.X()` scratch-temp declarations themselves, NOT the surrounding 74 lines of the same constructor (real state: this._climb/_roll/_slide/_dive/_cover/_worn/Map()/etc.), which are genuine state already represented by RollState/SlideState/DiveState/AirState/FlipState and this.worn-equivalent fields in FootAcrobatics.cs/FootController.cs/FootBelt.cs per their own existing citations.

foundNotFiled.reason_not_filed: Checked the concept-kept bar before filing an exclusion, per docs/port_units/README.md's explicit crane.js precedent ('Unity does this differently is not a supersession — check whether the port KEPT the concept first'), and it fails two different ways for the two halves of this range, so neither can be cleanly excluded as written: (1) the `frustumCulled = false` workaround (a Three.js bone-parented-mesh culling bug) genuinely has no Unity concept to port — SkinnedMeshRenderer bounds are recomputed from the live skeleton every frame, so this third of the range IS a clean exclusion candidate on its own. (2) the `loadWeapon(def)` async-download call is NOT absent as a concept — Combat/Pickups.cs already has `ILoader.LoadWeapon(WeaponDef def)` (Pickups.cs:292, called at :307) and Combat/WeaponAnimLoader.cs's own header explicitly says 'there is no loadWeapon() in this build yet' as an acknowledged open item, not a superseded one — so the concept was kept, just assigned to a different file/owner (Combat/*, not Character/FootBelt.cs, and not mine to edit this pass). FootBelt.cs's own `WearGear(string id, Transform obj, ...)` signature already takes the loaded Transform as a parameter rather than loading it itself, which is a reasonable Unity-side design (caller loads, then hands the result to WearGear) but means the literal 1061-1068 lines have no C# counterpart inside FootBelt.cs by design, not by omission — and the castShadow/receiveShadow half is ALREADY ported elsewhere (FootBelt.cs:838-839 sets ShadowCastingMode.On/receiveShadows=true on worn-gear renderers via its existing SkinBelt-family code path, confirmed by reading it this session). Net: nothing left to port or exclude inside FootBelt.cs itself; the one open question (should something call Pickups.ILoader.LoadWeapon before FootBelt.WearGear, the way foot.js's wearGear calls loadWeapon inline?) is a Core/Combat wiring decision outside this file's ownership, reported rather than guessed at.
